gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + SP037 400 W kit (1,920 Wh LiFePO4, 2,500 W, 1,000 W max solar input, one 400 W panel) costs $948 on ALLPOWERS' US store today. That is $251 less than the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 200 W kit ChatGPT picked ($1,199), with twice the panel wattage and 93% of the battery.
standout_why: I compared against backup-power.org (cited), energysage.com (cited), itechguides.com (cited, returned 502), blackoutwise.com (cited) and our own Nov 4 page. Goodhousekeeping.com (cited) could not be fetched. None of these lists any ALLPOWERS 2 kWh kit. backup-power.org gives only rounded prices from its own write-up ('around $1,550' for Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W; it is $1,499 today). EnergySage prices mostly cover the power station only. Blackoutwise gives price ranges dated Oct 9. ChatGPT's own DELTA 2 Max card showed $1,579, but EcoFlow lists it from $1,249 today. No rival compares 2 kWh kits on price per Wh with today's store prices.
decides: This challenges the pick. ChatGPT's own bar was a battery of about 2 kWh or more plus 400–800 W of panels. Measured against that bar today: the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 needs the 2×200 W kit at $1,499 ($0.72/Wh) or the 350 W kit at $1,449. The ALLPOWERS R2500 V2 + 400 W kit meets it at $948 ($0.49/Wh). The R2500 V2 kit becomes the value pick for a 2 kWh hurricane kit. The Elite 200 V2 stays the pick if a buyer wants the bigger maker and 2,600 W output. Before publishing, confirm the R2500 V2 kit's shipping date on its product page; the product endpoint was rate-limited.
